title: Faith precisely vs other virtues: simple assent habit in intellect alone
source_text: XXII. Ut autem recte fidei subjectum assignetur, notandum est fidem posse duplici modo sumi. Primo quidem praecise, prout spei & charitati, ac caeteris omnibus virtutibus opponitur. Et tum fides est unus simplex habitus, neque aliud quam firmus ac serius, & animum alte penetrans assensus, quem adhibemus Dei Verbo, & omnibus quae sunt in eo revelata. Fides hoc modo sumpta est in solo intellectu, nec ulla sui parte voluntati inhaeret. Nam veritati assensum praebere, intellectus est, non vero voluntatis. Et hactenus verum objectum intellectus, ut bonum voluntatis objectum habetur.
pass_a_gloss: But that faith's subject may be rightly assigned, it is to be noted that faith can be taken in a twofold way. First, precisely, as opposed to hope and charity and all other virtues. And then faith is one simple habit, nothing other than a firm and serious assent deeply penetrating the mind, which we give to God's Word and to all things revealed in it. Faith taken this way is in the intellect alone, and inheres in no part of itself in the will. For to give assent to truth belongs to intellect, not to will. And thus far the true is held the object of intellect, as the good is the object of will.
pass_b_english: Take faith precisely against hope/charity: one simple deep assent-habit to the Word.
So taken, seat is intellect alone — truth is intellect's object, good is will's.

lemmas.gloss: to be taken in a twofold way
